findings.summary: The regenerated report binds the stated worktree identity, completes all 49 matrix cells, sets runtimePass=true, and still keeps top-level pass/releasePass=false with releaseEvidenceEligible=false. This correctly prevents runtime success from becoming release eligibility.

The mobile and desktop entries mount separate owners, the manifest contains separate mobile/desktop scripts and styles selected by a loader, and the inspected phone, landscape, and tablet originals reflect deliberate responsive branches. Static ownership and asset-isolation checks passed.

package.json keeps check:route-supplement-contract in check:release-gates, but tools/check-route-supplement-contract.js reads the deleted src/panel-framework/mobile/mobile-domain.css and MobileDomainWorkspace.tsx. The command currently exits with ENOENT before checking the replacement telemetry owner, so the declared release gate is not runnable after this migration.
findings.action: Remove this retired validator from the release chain or port it to the mobile-telemetry owner and its styles; then run check:release-gates successfully. Retire or migrate the remaining package/tool validators that still name the deleted MobileDomainWorkspace and MobileInterfaceFocusContext owners.

findings.summary: The build now emits manifest v3 mobile/desktop assets and index.html references only panel-surface-loader, while .github/workflows/ci.yml still requires style.css, panel-framework.js, and content-addressed style.* / panel-framework.* references in index.html. Those legacy matches are absent from the new entry document, so the Windows packaging workflow will reject the migrated artifact.
findings.action: Replace the Windows CI assertions with manifest-v3 validation of the loader plus both declared mobile and desktop script/style assets, and update its legacy node --check target to the emitted surface assets.
